levers.name: ticket.get
levers.description: Read one service ticket for the client (synthetic PSA data).

impact.L1: A technician sees one person's ticket for this client; nothing about the person changes.
impact.L2: The client's ticket is read only by staff scoped to that client.
impact.L3: Every read is registered, scoped and audited, so the MSP can show who looked at what.
impact.L4: Client tickets never mix across tenants, so one office's problem is not another's exposure.

levers.name: kb.search
levers.description: Keyword search over the client's own knowledge base articles.

impact.L1: The person waiting on a fix gets an answer from their own client's articles, sooner.
impact.L2: Only the client's own knowledge base is searched; nothing changes in their tenant.
impact.L3: Technicians resolve repeat issues with the client's documented fix instead of guessing.
impact.L4: Answers stay inside each client's data, so retrieval never leaks between tenants.

levers.name: user.reset-mfa
levers.description: Remove a user's MFA methods (keeps the password) so they re-register at next sign-in. Mock of Graph authentication methods.

impact.L1: One person loses their MFA methods and must re-register at next sign-in; a wrong target or impostor locks them out or lets an attacker in.
impact.L2: The client's account security for one user changes; a social-engineered reset is a breach of client data.
impact.L3: An identity change the MSP must justify to auditors: verified requester, lead approval, audit record.
impact.L4: MFA resets are the step attackers talk their way through; doing it right at every client protects everyone.

levers.name: user.disable
levers.description: Disable a user account (accountEnabled = false). Mock of a Graph user update.

impact.L1: One person cannot sign in to anything until a technician re-enables the account.
impact.L2: The client loses that person's work until re-enabled; a wrong disable can stop a practice or desk.
impact.L3: An access change the MSP must justify to auditors: verified requester, lead approval, audit record.
impact.L4: Fast, correct offboarding and containment protect patients and investors; a wrong one erodes trust in automation.
